# PR Summary

Fix #11530

TraceVariableSet converts a value to string and if the value.ToString() throw the whole PowerShell expression is unexpectedly terminated. The fix is to catch the exception and return "null" string that is good for trace text output.

## PR Context

In #11530 Process.ToString() throws. Tracking issue for Process.ToString() https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/1520

pr_comments: I have never made a PR to PowerShell before so perhaps I am missing something, but how is it possible that this can only be tested interactively?
If there is a way to run a test for this (if need be we can run a child pwsh process to verify it doesn't crash when using this functionality) we should test this, absolutely. 👍

@jackhorton We have an edge case here because ToString methods should never throw but Process.ToString() throws if the process has terminated. Single negative impact is that script can break _only_ if we turn on debug. So it is never break mainstream and we can not fear regression.

# Steps to reproduce

```powershell
Set-PSDebug -Trace 2
$proc2 = Start-Process -FilePath sc.exe -PassThru -Wait
```

# Expected behavior

Same behavior as when PSDebug is at level 0; the (exited) process object is stored in `$proc2` and no crash occurs

# Actual behavior


review_comments: Hmm, I think the exception should be handled within `PSObject.ToStringParser`, where the `ToString()` method is called.

In debug/tracer we can mask any exception from ToString() without concern.
In engine code I am not sure that we can blindly do the same. 
Docs say that best practice is "avoid exceptions in ToString() methods". So we should consider this as a bug and we shouldn't mask this.
@daxian-dbw Could you please make a conclusion?

> Docs say that best practice is "avoid exceptions in ToString() methods". So we should consider this as a bug and we shouldn't mask this.

I agree with this, but I think it means we should fix the exception in `PSObject.ToStringParser()`
The PR is only for the trace code. For ToStringParser() we could have an issue with repo steps to discuss. It is not clear how many code paths we need to fix there if need.
It looks like this is always reassigned below, so the assignment is not needed
Unless this condition is reused elsewhere, it seems like we could just embed it into the `if (...)` condition directly, rather than assign it to a variable

This isn't really accurate -- the value isn't null, and our assumption is that this code path is reached in the event the object has been disposed (even though we catch any exception here).

Is `"null"` a string with a special meaning for us, or would something like `"<disposed>"` work just as well?
